papers.title: RFAmpDesigner: A Two-Level LLM-guided Optimization Framework for Automated Differential CMOS RF Amplifier Sizing
papers.abstract: Automated RF amplifier sizing is challenging because the design process is inherently hierarchical, the parameter space is high-dimensional and strongly coupled, and high-fidelity circuit simulation is expensive. Conventional optimization and reinforcement learning methods typically require many iterations and make limited use of RF domain knowledge, making them costly under tight simulation budgets. Large language models (LLMs) provide broad prior knowledge and reasoning capabilities, but are unreliable for direct numerical optimization. This paper presents RFAmpDesigner, a two-level optimization framework for automated schematic-level sizing of differential CMOS RF amplifiers. At the outer level, the circuit-parameter space is abstracted into a resource-allocation space, where LLMs make high-level allocation decisions and adjust them according to feedback from the inner level. At the inner level, RF design knowledge is used to decompose the flat sizing problem into a sequence of low-dimensional subproblems. Conventional optimizers then solve these subproblems to find circuit implementations consistent with the assigned resources. This structure allows numerical optimizers to focus on low-dimensional searches in the circuit-parameter space, while the LLM reasons and acts over a physically meaningful design space using simulation feedback. The main evaluation covers low-noise amplifier (LNA), driver amplifier (DA), and power amplifier (PA) designs within the target differential CMOS RF amplifier family. Experimental results show that it achieves a higher success rate under a limited simulation budget in both easy and hard regimes.

papers.title: A Meta-Research Review of Statistical Practices for Image-Reliant AI Tools Predicting Lung Cancer Outcomes
papers.abstract: AbstractAI models using medical images are increasingly proposed to support clinical decision-making in lung cancer, motivating assessment of their methodological rigor and transparency. To assess how these models are developed, evaluated, and reported, and to identify gaps in best statistical practices, we conducted a cross-sectional meta-research review of OpenAlex-indexed studies (January 1, 2023, to June 30, 2025) that developed image-based AI tools for lung cancer risk prediction, detection, or prognosis. Thirty-six studies met our inclusion criteria. Convolutional neural networks were used in most studies (27 studies, 75%), and area under the curve (AUC) was the most frequently reported evaluation metric (29 studies, 81%). Although 23 studies (64%) reported some form of uncertainty quantification, most were limited to presenting confidence intervals for global performance metrics (e.g., AUC, sensitivity, and accuracy) rather than individual prediction- or risk-level uncertainty. Common limitations included limited external test set use (14 studies, 39%), insufficient subgroup analyses (10 studies, 28%), and limited adherence to established prediction-model reporting guidelines. Overall, future research should prioritize standardized reporting, use of external test sets, and model performance assessment across clinically relevant subpopulations. The coexistence of increasingly powerful AI-based prediction models with inconsistent study design, evaluation, and reporting practices emphasizes the urgent need to implement more rigorous and transparent methodological standards in this field. (Funded by Yale School of Public Health.).

papers.title: A robotics- and machine learning-integrated workflow for discovering all-natural plastic substitutes
papers.abstract: The global accumulation of nondegradable petrochemical plastic waste is driving the search for biodegradable substitutes derived from natural resources. However, discovering all-natural composite materials that match the optical, thermal and mechanical performance of commercial plastics remains challenging because traditional iterative optimization is inefficient. Here the workflow described in this Protocol accelerates the screening process by using automated robotics for liquid handing and machine learning to predict material properties. The procedure begins by commanding a pipetting robot to prepare a library of 286 nanocomposites. Basic physical properties of these products are used to train a support vector machine classifier that locates the decision boundary separating feasible from infeasible film compositions in the four-component system, thereby defining the feasible design space. Next, through 14 active learning loops coupled with data augmentation (for example, adding small random changes to the characterization data within the observed experimental error range), the robot fabricates 135 all-natural nanocomposites in a stagewise manner to construct an artificial neural network prediction model. The model is used to predict (1) the physicochemical properties of a nanocomposite from its composition and (2) which compositions are likely to have the desired, user-specified properties (for example, transparency or fire resistance). This protocol further details methods for model interpretation using Shapley Additive Explanations, validation via molecular dynamics simulations and model expansion to incorporate new building blocks. This hybrid approach takes ~2 months and enables the accelerated discovery of eco-friendly materials with programmable functions using components drawn from the generally recognized as safe database. There is an urgent need for greener alternatives to plastics. This Protocol describes a rational combination of machine learning with experimental data to explore the feasible design space of plastic substitutes made from all-natural composites.

papers.title: Ejector-performance-oriented model predictive control of MED-TVC systems under motive steam pressure disturbances
papers.abstract: This study addresses the challenge of maintaining high steam utilization efficiency in Multi-Effect Distillation with Thermal Vapor Compression (MED-TVC) systems under motive steam pressure disturbances. Owing to the high sensitivity of conventional fixed-geometry ejector entrainment performance to off-design pressure conditions, conventional temperature regulation strategies can maintain process stability but are generally unable to prevent the ejector from deviating from its optimal high-efficiency operating region. Consequently, system thermal efficiency may deteriorate under pressure disturbances. To address this problem, an ejector-performance-oriented model predictive control (EPO-MPC) strategy is proposed. The strategy combines a dynamic MED model, a data-driven ejector model constructed from computational fluid dynamics (CFD) data and thin-plate-spline (TPS) interpolation, and an ejector-performance-oriented setpoint optimizer embedded in a constrained MPC framework. The optimizer updates the final-effect evaporator temperature setpoint in real time so that the ejector remains close to its high-entrainment double-choked region. Simulations under motive steam pressure variations from 900 to 1300 kPa show that the EPO-MPC achieves a higher entrainment ratio (ER) and gain output ratio (GOR) compared to the PID controller and conventional MPC. The practical efficacy of the EPO-MPC is further validated through physical experiments. Results show that, compared to the PID and conventional MPC, the EPO-MPC achieves a 3.53% and 1.55% increase in GOR under realistic steam pressure fluctuations.

papers.title: LoRa-Based Multi-Hop Network for Smart Water Metering Devices
papers.abstract: Smart water metering requires low-power, large-scale communication that existing LPWAN solutions do not fully address: the single-hop topology of LoRaWAN needs dense gateway deployments in urban environments, and cellular alternatives incur subscription costs and higher energy consumption. This paper presents a multi-hop LoRa protocol for smart water metering that exploits the static topology and uplink-dominated traffic of this application to simplify the protocol design. Each node selects its relay through a lightweight message exchange and a cost function that weights hop count, relay load and link quality, using only local information, so that the network forms a tree rooted at the gateway. Overhearing the relay retransmission replaces dedicated acknowledgement packets on the relayed hops. The cost function coefficients were tuned by Bayesian optimization for networks of up to 100 nodes; the best configuration depends on network size, and the link-quality weight proved negligible. On topologies not used for tuning, with node density increasing over a fixed area, the mean peak relay load settles at 13.6 to 15.2 clients for 40 to 100 nodes, a reduction of up to 67% relative to a shortest-hop (BFS) baseline, for an average hop-count increase of up to 13.5%. The transmit energy of the busiest relay falls by up to 69%, although its daily consumption remains dominated by reception. The evaluation covers the topology produced by relay selection and the resulting analytical energy budget.

papers.title: Carbon quota compensation mechanism for deep peak regulation of thermal power units to enhance renewable energy accommodation
papers.abstract: During deep peak regulation, thermal power units face increased low-carbon compliance pressure because carbon-emission intensity rises non-linearly at low loads. Existing studies generally rely on fixed emission factors or simplified linear models and fail to characterize carbon-quota surpluses and deficits under current settlement policies or provide compensation mechanisms for flexible thermal-power regulation. In this study, we propose a carbon quota compensation mechanism to enhance renewable energy accommodation. First, a full-operating-condition carbon-emission model is established considering non-linear emission-intensity variation and the startup/shutdown rebound effect. Analysis based on this model reveals that carbon emissions may decrease while carbon quota demand increases during deep peak regulation. Second, a dynamic green certificate–carbon quota conversion coefficient is derived by matching additional carbon quota demand with incremental renewable energy accommodation, establishing a physically interpretable linkage between convertible green certificates and dedicated carbon offsets. Finally, a multi-time-scale rolling optimization and compensation strategy is developed based on model predictive control. Annual, monthly, and daily operations are coordinated through dynamic environmental-rights inventories, rolling updates, and ex post compensation accounting, thereby incorporating long-term environmental costs into short-term scheduling. Case studies demonstrate that the proposed mechanism alleviates deep peak-regulation pressure on thermal power units, improves renewable energy accommodation, and enhances the low-carbon economic performance of the power system.

papers.title: Prediction of coronary artery disease from non-invasive test reports and demographic characteristics using calibrated ensemble learning
papers.abstract: Coronary artery disease (CAD) is commonly confirmed using invasive or imaging-based investigations, motivating transparent prediction from routinely collected clinical information. We analysed 920 records from the Cleveland, Hungarian, Switzerland, and VA Long Beach cohorts of the UCI Heart Disease database. The binary endpoint was absence versus presence of angiographic heart disease. Missing continuous and categorical variables were imputed within training folds, together with fold-contained encoding, scaling, and probability calibration. A stratified split produced 644 development and 276 untouched evaluation records. The primary ensemble averaged sigmoid-calibrated probabilities from K-nearest neighbours, logistic regression, and a support-vector classifier. It achieved accuracy 0.8297, sensitivity 0.8824, specificity 0.7642, precision 0.8232, F1-score 0.8517, AUROC 0.8840, average precision 0.8867, and Brier score 0.1325. A focused comparison of Extra Trees, gradient boosting, histogram gradient boosting, weighted blending, and probability stacking showed that the strongest deterministic and probabilistic models differed: SVC achieved accuracy 0.8333, whereas a constrained blend achieved AUROC 0.8883 and Brier score 0.1299. Permutation importance and Monte Carlo SHAP explanations identified chest-pain type, exercise-induced ST depression, exercise-induced angina, and thallium-test results as influential contributors. Leave-one-cohort-out AUROC ranged from 0.7152 to 0.9011. The combined framework integrates calibrated ensembling, uncertainty quantification, patient-level explanation, and cohort-aware validation for non-invasive CAD prediction.

papers.title: Density functional theory and Bayesian optimization for therapeutic discovery
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: ) with system size. Bayesian Optimization-guided Density Functional Theory resolves this by embedding quantum-accurate property evaluation within a probabilistic active learning loop that directs computational resources toward maximally informative candidates. AREAS COVERED: The authors critically examine DFT functional selection, basis set adequacy, and scaling mitigation strategies for drug-like molecules, alongside Bayesian Optimization surrogate architectures, acquisition function design, and multi-fidelity extensions spanning GFN2-xTB to DLPNO-CCSD(T). A quantitative structured comparative synthesis of eleven published DFT-BO campaigns is presented, and integration strategies, including sequential, batch, and surrogate-assisted pipelines, are analyzed. This review is based on a structured literature search conducted in PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and Google Scholar, covering publications from 1965 to July 2026. EXPERT OPINION: The convergence of fault-tolerant quantum computing, large-scale molecular foundation models, and exascale hardware is expected to broaden the scope of DFT-BO integration. We argue that the value of these methods is presently established for the optimization of quantum-chemical properties rather than for therapeutic endpoints, and we identify the benchmarking and validation evidence that would be required to establish the latter.

papers.title: Parameter identifiability and uncertainty quantification in a delayed within-host HIV dynamical model
papers.abstract: Accurate parameter inference in within-host viral infection models is frequently hindered by parameter coupling and limited observability, particularly when only viral-load data are available. In this study, we investigate structural and practical identifiability, posterior uncertainty, model adequacy, and predictive robustness in a delayed within-host HIV dynamics framework that incorporates intracellular infection latency. Using simulated longitudinal viral-load data, we combine differential-elimination analysis, profile likelihood, Bayesian posterior inference, information-theoretic model comparison, variance-based global sensitivity analysis, and forward uncertainty propagation. Under the known nonzero history functions used in the synthetic design, differential elimination establishes generic local structural identifiability of the seven model parameters and makes explicit the parameter combinations entering the viral-load observation map. Re-optimized profile likelihoods for the infection-rate parameter and the infected-cell death-rate parameter both cross the 95% likelihood-ratio threshold on either side of their minima, giving bounded intervals. The infection-rate profile is nevertheless broader and more asymmetric, indicating weaker practical constraint rather than practical non-identifiability. A conditional three-parameter, four-chain Bayesian analysis yields concentrated marginal posterior distributions for the infection-rate, virion-production, and intracellular-delay parameters, with split R-hat values no larger than 1.005 and pooled effective sample sizes between 935 and 1398. However, the infection-rate and virion-production parameters show a very strong negative posterior correlation of approximately −0.994, revealing substantial compensatory dependence that is not apparent from marginal credible intervals alone. Within the matched synthetic benchmark, the delayed formulation is favored over a reduced non-delayed alternative by both the Akaike Information Criterion and Bayesian Information Criterion, although this comparison is interpreted as a model-recovery experiment rather than external validation because the data were generated from the delayed model. Global sensitivity analysis identifies the infected-cell death rate and viral clearance rate as the strongest contributors to equilibrium viral-load variability, with the virion-production rate and target-cell production rate showing intermediate effects, whereas predictive uncertainty is greatest during the transient growth and peak phase. These findings show that trajectory fit alone is insufficient for reliable mechanistic inference and that structural identifiability, practical likelihood geometry, joint posterior dependence, and predictive robustness should be evaluated together.

papers.abstract: This research aimed to: (1) examine the current and desirable conditions and priority needs for happy school administration; (2) develop a happy school administration model; and (3) evaluate the developed model for schools under the Prachuap Khiri Khan Primary Educational Service Area Office 2. The study employed a research and development design comprising three phases. In Phase 1, the sample consisted of 292 school administrators and teachers selected through multistage and simple random sampling. Data were collected using a five-point rating-scale questionnaire with a reliability coefficient of 0.986 and analyzed using frequency, percentage, mean, standard deviation, and the Modified Priority Needs Index (PNI_modified). In Phase 2, the model was developed based on qualitative data obtained from nine key informants: four educational administrators, two school administrators, and three academics. In Phase 3, nine experts evaluated the model in terms of accuracy, utility, feasibility, and propriety. The findings revealed that: (1) the overall priority need for happy school administration was high (PNImodified = 1.09). The development priorities were creative leadership and educational administration, active learning and positive psychology, teacher quality and workplace well-being, learner quality and collaborative networks, and physical and psychosocial environments, respectively. (2) The developed CATLS Model comprised five components: Creative Leadership and Educational Administration (C), Active Learning Process and Positive Psychology (A), Teacher Quality and Workplace Well-Being (T), Learner Quality and Collaborative Networks (L), and Safe Physical and Psychosocial Environments (S). (3) The overall evaluation of the model was at the highest level (x̄ = 4.82, S.D. = 0.33).

papers.title: Team-based learning in pharmacology: insights into student perceptions and assessment outcomes from a quasi-experimental study
papers.abstract: Background Active learning approaches, particularly team-based learning (TBL), are increasingly used within medical education to promote collaborative learning. However, evidence comparing TBL with traditional didactic lectures (TDL) in pharmacology remains mixed, particularly regarding immediate learning gains and student perceptions. This study compared TBL and TDL among fourth-year medical students, examining learning gains, gender differences, perceptions, and the relationship between perceptions and relative learning gains. Methods In this quasi-experimental study, 137 of 223 students completed the pre-test, post-test, and perception questionnaire. Topic-specific 10-item multiple-choice tests were administered immediately before and after each session. Perceptions were evaluated using a 29-item Likert-scale questionnaire. Changes in assessment scores were calculated using repeated-measures analysis of variance, and associations between perceptions and relative learning gains were examined using Spearman's rank-order correlations. Results Assessment scores considerably improved from pre-test to post-test in both groups ( p < 0.001). Although the mean learning gain was slightly greater with TBL, the Method × Time interaction was not significant ( p = 0.145), and there was no significant difference in gain scores between TBL and TDL ( p = 0.100). The difference in learning gains between TBL and TDL did not vary significantly by gender ( p = 0.079), and perceptions did not differ by gender. Perception domains were intercorrelated but were not significantly associated with the relative difference in TBL and TDL learning gains. Conclusion Both TBL and TDL improved immediate pharmacology knowledge, with no significant difference in learning gains between approaches. TBL was favorably perceived by students. Further research is warranted to examine longer-term and broader educational outcomes.

papers.title: Effectiveness of Flipped Classroom versus Modified Team-Based Learning with Tutorial on Clinical Competency in Physiotherapy Education: A Mixed-Methods Study
papers.abstract: Physiotherapy education is progressively moving away from traditional lecture-based approaches and is focusing on active learning strategies within competency-based frameworks. In this article, we explored which method, flipped classroom with tutorials or modified team-based learning with tutorials, is more effective in developing the clinical competency of final-year physiotherapy students. In total, 82 students participated in this study, which was designed as a parallel group experiment. They were randomly assigned to one of two groups (n = 41 per group). The intervention lasted for four weeks. The flipped classroom group learned the main concepts online before coming to the class. At the tutorials, they discussed their knowledge and performed interactive tasks. The modified team-based learning group participated in structured teamwork, including readiness assurance tests and application exercises, in addition to the tutorials. We evaluated clinical competencies using pre- and post-intervention weighted learning gain scores and gathered qualitative data from reflective journals. Both pedagogical interventions were beneficial to clinical competency results. However, the modified team-based learning group not only outperformed the other group in the post-intervention examination but also recorded greater learning gains. The mean weighted learning gain in the modified team-based learning group was 72.10%, whereas that in the flipped classroom group was 63.07%. Qualitative data revealed that learner autonomy was supported, analytical thinking was facilitated, and collaborative learning was strengthened in both groups; however, these effects were stronger in the modified team-based learning group. These findings suggest that incorporating collaborative, team-based methods alongside tutorial support could be a good way to improve clinical competency in physiotherapy education. Additional studies with larger samples and longer follow-up periods are required.

papers.title: Prioritization of Rental Vehicle Fleet Maintenance: From Predictive Condition Indexes to Autonomous Intervention Solutions
papers.abstract: Predictive maintenance research for vehicle fleets has advanced substantially in health index construction, remaining useful life (RUL) estimation, and uncertainty quantification. The operational translation of these outputs into scheduling decisions has received comparatively little structured attention in rental and car-sharing contexts. A rental vehicle changes drivers with every transaction, and its technical condition must be reconciled with reservation calendars, geographic coverage, and revenue considerations that have no analogue in owner-operated or logistics fleets. This paper synthesizes prognostics, health management, and fleet-optimization literature to characterize the gap between condition-index generation and autonomous intervention scheduling. Existing approaches are organized by the degree of operational context integration, the decision mechanism employed, and the scale at which validation has been reported. A composite scoring framework for rental fleets, validated across 847 vehicles and 2.31 million vehicle-hours of operation, is examined as the only located case combining all four rental-specific context variables into a single computable score. Condition-index generation has matured faster than the scheduling logic needed to act on it. Interoperability and data-governance constraints form the primary barrier to deployment at scale.

papers.title: Bearing-grouped, stage-resolved uncertainty assessment for remaining useful life prediction of rolling bearings
papers.abstract: Abstract Accurate prediction of the remaining useful life of rolling bearings is important for reducing downtime costs and ensuring system safety. However, existing data-driven methods still face severe challenges, such as large sensor noise interference, non-monotonic degradation indicators, and the lack of reliable confidence intervals for point prediction results. This paper proposes a bearing RUL uncertainty quantification prediction framework that integrates robust health indicators construction, bidirectional long short-term memory network and inductive conformal prediction. First, the method smooths and accumulates the vibration signals to construct a strictly monotonic health indicator that conforms to the irreversible physical characteristics to suppress random fluctuations. Then, it uses the BiLSTM network to capture bidirectional temporal evolution features and achieve high-precision mapping from degradation features to RUL. Finally, it introduces the conformal prediction theory, which quantifies the prediction risk without assuming the error distribution, and uses an independent calibration set to construct a prediction interval with strict statistical coverage guarantee for the predicted values. The experimental results on the PHM IEEE 2012 and XJTU-SY datasets show that in terms of the root mean square error and mean absolute error metrics, the proposed method significantly outperforms traditional models.Furthermore, the coverage probability of the prediction interval remains above 95% to ensure high prediction accuracy and reliable uncertainty quantification capability. The study shows that it can provide a theoretically sound and technically supported basis for state-based maintenance decisions in complex industrial scenarios with high credibility, by combining physical monotonicity constraint and statistical calibration.

papers.title: Hierarchical active learning for annotation-efficient 3D object detection in construction-scene LiDAR sensing
papers.abstract: 3D object detection in construction-scene LiDAR sensing remains challenging because sparse returns, irregular layouts, heavy occlusion, and diverse machinery make object representation and localization difficult. Dense manual annotation in such scenes is also inefficient and costly, creating a strong need for annotation-efficient learning. Existing active-learning methods often struggle in this setting because they tend to favor uncertain but redundant samples while overlooking representative scene coverage. To address this problem, we propose Hierarchical Clustering-enhanced Active Learning (HCAL), an active-learning framework for LiDAR-based 3D object detection in construction and roadwork environments. HCAL improves sample selection under limited labeling budgets by identifying informative candidate keyframes, suppressing redundant uncertain samples, and preserving representative coverage through entropy filtering, gradient-space clustering, and density-consistency selection. To support field-relevant evaluation, we further establish ConVeh3D as a construction-scene LiDAR benchmark for annotation-efficient 3D detection and unknown-category-aware evaluation in a controlled category-withheld setting. Experiments on ConVeh3D, with KITTI as secondary supporting evidence, show that HCAL achieves the best average detection accuracy across most tested labeling budgets. The results indicate that HCAL provides an effective framework for improving sample efficiency in construction-scene LiDAR-based 3D object detection under limited labeling budgets. The dataset and code will be made available at https://github.com/zxk688/ConVeh3D .

papers.title: Review of applications of artificial intelligence in bioimpedance analysis
papers.abstract: Bioimpedance analysis serves as a non-invasive modality for evaluating human body composition and fluid balance. Despite its clinical translational potential, traditional empirical regression models remain vulnerable to physiological variability, demographic heterogeneity, and measurement noise, which inflate estimation error and restrict generalizability. In this review, we present an evidence-based narrative synthesis of artificial intelligence (AI) methodologies integrated into bioimpedance frameworks to investigate these limitations. We analyzed how machine learning algorithms optimize non-linear Cole parameter extraction and equivalent circuit modeling under noisy spectral conditions without requiring rigid baseline assumptions. Furthermore, deep learning architectures such as convolutional networks and physics-informed models were examined for their capacity to resolve ill-posed inverse reconstruction problems in electrical impedance tomography and to process multidimensional sensor streams. Rather than presuming established clinical maturity, we critically scrutinized study-level translational readiness, highlighting pervasive methodological bottlenecks, including the reliance on small, single-center cohorts, risks of data leakage from sample-level cross-validation, hardware-induced motion artifacts, and an absence of independent external multicenter replication. By contextualizing emerging paradigms, including Explainable AI, uncertainty quantification, and decentralized learning within a realistic clinical taxonomy, we outline the methodological and validation standards necessary to advance AI-driven bioimpedance from exploratory proof-of-concept demonstrations toward reproducible, evidence-based clinical evaluation.

papers.title: Rapid FE-informed surrogate benchmarking for peak-temperature sequence prediction in Ti-6Al-4V laser-directed energy deposition
papers.abstract: Purpose This study aims to benchmark next-state reconstruction of one FE-generated scalar peak-temperature sequence for Ti-6Al-4V laser-directed energy deposition (L-DED) as a methodological study, not a deployment-ready process model. Design/methodology/approach A conduction-dominated 10-layer wall was simulated in ANSYS Workbench Mechanical APDL 2025 R1 with temperature-dependent properties, layer activation, a Goldak-type source and convective-radiative losses. The 823-state sequence compared LSTM, XGBoost and DNN using a common target, 20-state context, chronological split, training-only scaling, scoring convention and CPU timing; model-specific inputs are documented. Findings Across the 803-state prediction region, XGBoost achieved RMSE = 12.36 K and MAE = 7.80 K; in the 165-state late validation interval, these rose to 24.58 K and 21.14 K. Cycle- and phase-resolved diagnostics localized the strongest degradation to late-build and rapid heating/near-peak states. XGBoost gave the best accuracy-cost compromise for this data set. Research limitations/implications The high accuracy is strictly an intra-case interpolation result for one FE-generated sequence, not evidence of cross-condition generalization or experimental fidelity. Latent heat and thermo-fluid melt-pool flow are excluded. Practical implications The present model supports only FE-sequence reconstruction and offline algorithm screening. Practical use requires matched experiments, multi-condition training, uncertainty quantification and validation of the complete sensing-control pipeline. Originality/value The transferable protocol combines target-time splitting, training-only preprocessing, explicit context exclusion, documented model-specific features, layer/phase diagnostics and amortized latency reporting, exposing degradation hidden by global R2.

papers.title: Three-Step Continuous-Flow Synthesis of GABA from an L-Carnitine Byproduct: Integrating Inline FTIR and Bayesian Optimization for Rapid Process Development
papers.abstract: Abstract We report a three-step telescoped continuous-flow synthesis of γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) starting from ethyl 4-hydroxycrotonate (EHC), a stoichiometric byproduct generated during L-carnitine production. The route proceeds through azidation with DPPA/DBU, dual-site catalytic hydrogenation over a Pd/C fixed bed, and alkaline ester hydrolysis. All three steps are conducted in a fully integrated flow system with no intermediate isolation required. A key engineering challenge, salt-induced microchannel clogging during quenching of the azidation step, was resolved with a 22 wt % subsaturated NH4Cl solution, which simultaneously suppresses clogging and maintains stable liquid–liquid phase separation. The hydrogenation step, which must reduce both the C═C bond and the azide group in a single pass, was optimized over a five-variable parameter space using multiobjective Bayesian optimization with Gaussian process surrogate models, guided by inline FTIR spectroscopy. Starting from five Latin hypercube initialization points, the hypervolume appeared to plateau after only 21 total experiments. The three-step telescoped process delivers GABA in 75.1% overall yield. This study demonstrates how a structurally defined industrial byproduct can be valorized through a combination of inherently safe continuous-flow processing and data-driven optimization, with particular relevance to systems operating in uncharted parameter spaces under hazardous intermediate constraints.

papers.title: From Classical Control to Deep Reinforcement Learning: A Reproducible Framework for Quadrotor Modeling and Control
papers.abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles used in delivery applications must maintain reliable trajectory tracking despite payload variations that alter the vehicle dynamics. This study compares seven control strategies—proportional–integral–derivative (PID), linear quadratic regulator (LQR), linear quadratic integral (LQI), linear model predictive control (MPC), nonlinear MPC (NMPC), Adaptive NMPC, and Soft Actor–Critic (SAC)—for a nonlinear quadrotor under nominal conditions, staged payload-mass variation, and measurement noise. All controllers are evaluated using the same vehicle model, actuator constraints, and four benchmark trajectories. The comparison considers tracking accuracy, robustness, estimated mechanical propulsion power, actuator saturation, benchmark completion, noise sensitivity, and computational burden. Under nominal conditions, NMPC and Adaptive NMPC achieve nearly identical tracking, with a maximum difference in three-dimensional root-mean-square error (3D RMSE) of approximately 4.5 × 10−4 m. Under staged payload-mass variation, Adaptive NMPC completes all four trajectories without divergence, whereas fixed-model NMPC remains bounded only in Hover and diverges on the three moving trajectories. In the Hover case, adaptation reduces the 3D RMSE by 80.2% (from 0.3085 m to 0.0611 m). SAC exhibits pronounced trajectory- and seed-dependent performance; the representative policy (Seed 1) completes only 3 of the 8 nominal and staged-mass benchmarks at full duration. These results demonstrate that strong nominal tracking alone does not guarantee robustness to payload variation, and they highlight the benefit of online model adaptation for quadrotor control under changing mass conditions.

papers.title: Disturbance prediction-based tube-MPC path tracking control method for autonomous vehicles
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a disturbance prediction-based Tube Model Predictive Control (PTMPC) method to address the degradation of path tracking accuracy in autonomous vehicles under complex operating conditions caused by nonlinear attenuation of tire cornering stiffness and external disturbances. First, an inverse dynamics-based tire cornering stiffness deviation prediction model is constructed to predict tire stiffness deviations and establish a mapping from stiffness deviations to system state perturbations, thereby transforming parameter uncertainties into bounded state disturbances. Secondly, the minimal robust invariant set is computed offline using disturbance boundaries, combined with online receding-horizon optimization and constraint tightening to dynamically compensate for external disturbances. Finally, CarSim/Simulink co-simulation results demonstrate that by integrating disturbance prediction with robust set optimization, PTMPC significantly enhances control accuracy and stability under complex disturbance conditions.

papers.title: Advances in algorithm‑driven tomographic volumetric (bio)printing toward an AI‑led future
papers.abstract: Abstract Tomographic volumetric printing (TVP) is an emerging three-dimensional (3D) technique that enables rapid, layer-free fabrication of sophisticated structures via multi-angle light projection. While tomographic volumetric bioprinting (TVBP) extends to print with living cells, allowing for fast fabrication of cell-laden 3D constructs. Our continuous work and the rapid developments on TVP/TVBP (TV(B)P) encourage us to review the current challenges faced by TV(B)P and the recent trend in algorithm-based optimization vs AI-based optimization. This review summarizes recent algorithmic advances in TV(B)P, with emphasis on algorithmic strategies for improving printing resolution and fidelity, including optimization of light refraction, scattering, and iterative reconstruction. Then, we further explore increasing attention on the emergence of AI-based TV(B)P, enabling automatic parameter optimization, adaptive exposure control, accelerated slicing, and automated quality assessment. Further, we compare the differences between algorithm-based and AI-based strategies, as well as the difference between AI-driven TV(B)P, by which the system is granted autonomous decision-making power at critical stages of manufacturing; and AI-assisted TV(B)P, by which efficiency, robustness, and interpretability are enhanced without replacing existing physical or algorithmic models. In summary, this review offers insights into the future directions of AI-based TV(B)P in materials science, biomedical engineering, and advanced manufacturing.

papers.title: Data-driven predictive control of battery energy storage with physics-informed sequence modeling
papers.abstract: Integrating battery energy storage systems (BESS) into industrial sites with photovoltaic generation and time-varying tariffs requires controllers that combine economic performance, low real-time computational cost, and robustness to forecast errors. Model predictive control (MPC) achieves near-optimal cost but solves a mixed-integer optimization at every step using a linearized battery model, since nonlinear formulations are intractable for real-time deployment. Learning-based controllers remove this online optimization, but they are typically trained without any knowledge of the equipment they operate on; they are tuned site by site, and they provide no structural guarantee that operational constraints will be met. Closing this gap is the motivation of this work. This paper proposes PI-DT, a data-driven predictive controller based on a transformer sequence model conditioned on the return-to-go, trained offline on linear MILP expert actions executed on a nonlinear Thévenin two-branch RC battery simulator, and informed by per-battery physics, so that a single network operates batteries of different capacity, rated power, and efficiency without per-site retraining. An asymmetric minimum terminal state of charge (SOC) constraint, closer to industrial practice than a fixed target, is enforced consistently across expert, MPC, and the proposed controller, and enforced at inference through a horizon-aware projection on the action. The evaluation uses the public EMSx dataset (60 industrial sites, 37,442 site-days, Spanish PVPC tariff) and compares against the Rolling MPC, behavior cloning (BC), and Implicit Q-Learning (IQL), all assessed under the same nonlinear battery dynamics. On 5577 test site-days, the proposed controller reaches an aggregate cost gap of 1.39% versus the MILP, below 1.54% (BC), 1.61% (MPC), and 1.96% (IQL). The learning baselines fall below the minimum terminal SOC by up to 8.4 and 29 percentage points, respectively; the projection makes the reserve feasible by construction under the linear SOC model on which it is computed, and on the nonlinear plant the worst-case residual deficit of the proposed controller is 0.14 pp, within the 1 pp operational tolerance. A 3-fold cross-validation on held-out sites shows it transfers to unseen batteries with negligible degradation. The proposed controller therefore attains MPC-level economics without an online solver and with a structurally enforced end-of-day reserve, which makes it a candidate for embedded deployment in industrial energy management systems, subject to hardware-in-the-loop validation.

papers.title: The ‘four-pillar’ construct for failed subtrochanteric osteosynthesis: a standardised reconstructive framework and preliminary clinical and radiological outcomes
papers.abstract: Abstract Background To describe a standardised four-pillar reconstructive framework for conversion to total hip arthroplasty (THA) after failed subtrochanteric fracture fixation, and to report preliminary short- to mid-term clinical and radiological outcomes. Materials and methods We retrospectively reviewed patients aged > 60 years who underwent cementless conversion THA according to a four-pillar reconstructive framework for failed subtrochanteric fracture fixation between January 2017 and December 2024. All patients had previously been treated with an intramedullary nail. The framework addressed four predefined domains: distal axial and rotational fixation, joint stability, reconstruction of the trochanteric-abductor complex and preservation or restoration of medial cortical support. Clinical outcomes were assessed using the Harris Hip Score (HHS) and a visual analogue scale (VAS) for pain. Serial radiographs were reviewed for stem fixation, clinically relevant migration, healing at the subtrochanteric reconstruction site and cortical strut allograft behaviour where applicable. Results Fifteen patients constituted the final outcome-analysis cohort [mean age 72.7 years (SD 4.0); mean follow-up 23.7 months; median 24 months (IQR 18–30; range 12–36)]. A trochanteric grip plate was used in all patients, and a tibial cortical strut allograft was used in 9 of 15 patients in whom the operative report documented a relevant medial or anteromedial cortical deficiency. Mean operative time was 101 min (SD 30.5), and full weight-bearing was achieved at a mean of 6.8 weeks (SD 1.2). Mean HHS increased from 42 (SD 9) to 80 (SD 7), and mean VAS pain score decreased from 8.0 (SD 0.8) to 2.0 (SD 0.8). No stem showed clinically relevant subsidence (> 5 mm) or progressive radiolucent lines. One major postoperative complication, a pulmonary embolism requiring temporary intensive care unit admission, and two minor complications were documented; no patient in the final outcome cohort required reoperation or revision surgery during the available follow-up. Conclusions Cementless conversion THA performed according to a four-pillar reconstructive framework was associated with favourable early clinical and radiological outcomes in this retrospective series. Larger prospective comparative studies with longer follow-up are required to determine whether this framework provides advantages over alternative reconstructive strategies. Level of evidence IV (retrospective case series; Oxford Centre for Evidence-Based Medicine 2011 Levels of Evidence).

papers.title: A Hard-Constrained PINN Framework for Variable-Coefficient Identification in the Two-Dimensional Sine-Gordon Equation
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a hard-constrained dual-branch physics-informed neural network (PINN) framework for identifying unknown variable coefficients in the two-dimensional sine-Gordon equation. Three prescribed classes of coefficients are considered, including time-dependent, space-dependent, and spatiotemporally varying coefficients. The framework uses a state network and a coefficient network to reconstruct the state field and the unknown coefficient simultaneously. A hard-constrained trial solution is constructed to satisfy the initial displacement, initial velocity, and Dirichlet boundary conditions analytically. Residual-based adaptive refinement and coefficient smoothness regularization are further incorporated to improve the empirical inversion behavior in the tested settings. Numerical experiments are conducted on a unit-square domain with known source terms and prescribed initial-boundary data. The results show that the time-dependent and space-dependent coefficients can be recovered with relative coefficient errors mainly on the order of 10−2, whereas the fully spatiotemporal coefficient case is more challenging, with relative errors on the order of 10−1. Ablation studies, noise and observation-sensitivity tests, inverse-PINN baseline comparisons, and an independent forward-solve benchmark are provided to assess the behavior of the method. The study is restricted to controlled numerical settings with known forcing and prescribed Dirichlet data. Extensions to irregular geometries, mixed boundary conditions, model-form errors, real measurements, and large-scale implementations remain topics for future work.

papers.title: Radiation cavity design and optimization of radioisotope thermophotovoltaic systems
papers.abstract: Radiation cavity design in radioisotope thermophotovoltaic (RTPV) systems is constrained by the compact geometry of the General-Purpose Heat Source (GPHS) module and the coupling among radiative heat transfer, thermal insulation, and photovoltaic conversion. Seven radiation cavity configurations with different power-generating surface arrangements are developed and evaluated. The results show that RTPV performance is governed by the coupled interaction among the radiative power received by the photovoltaic cell, filter absorption, net radiative heat transfer through the thermal insulation, and residual radiative energy rather than by any single structural parameter. The system efficiency of the seven configurations ranges from 24.58% to 27.78%, and the structure with a six-sided emitter, a single-sided cell, and five-sided thermal insulation is selected for further optimization. A physics-informed multi-scale attention framework is then proposed for rapid parameter optimization. The attention multi-layer perceptron (Att-MLP) predicts intermediate physical variables, while the multi-scale residual physics-informed neural network (MSR-PINN) predicts system efficiency by integrating data-driven learning with physical models. The framework achieves an R 2 of 0.9729, an MAE of 0.0014, and an RMSE of 0.0022. Independent L-BFGS-B and dual-annealing searches identify a candidate with a predicted efficiency of 31.72%, compared with 31.75% from photovoltaic calculations using COMSOL-derived quantities. Relative differences in the intermediate quantities are below 1.49%, supporting cavity optimization within the selected topology and prescribed conditions.

papers.title: Model Predictive Guidance Applied to Planetary Entry and Powered Descent
papers.abstract: Trajectory tracking is central to planetary entry, descent, and landing (EDL) missions, where reference trajectories must be followed closely in the presence of dispersions and system and environmental uncertainties. Traditional gain-scheduled controllers require laborious offline tuning, do not systematically enforce constraints, and lack rigorous closed-loop stability guarantees. A recently developed model predictive guidance (MPG) method inherits the strengths of model predictive control and addresses these challenges while avoiding the need for an onboard conventional quadratic programming solver. This paper provides detailed applications of the MPG method in EDL. The method is demonstrated in lunar powered descent, Mars powered descent, and Mars atmospheric entry of human-scale EDL missions. The results show accurate tracking, effective constraint enforcement, and low computational overhead consistent with real-time onboard implementation. These results establish MPG as a practical, effective, and computationally efficient tracking guidance approach for planetary EDL missions.

papers.title: Designing metacognitive scaffolding in flipped learning to enhance students’ visual–spatial reasoning: Evidence from geometry instruction
papers.abstract: The development of students’ visual–spatial reasoning is a persistent challenge in geometry learning, where abstract representations and spatial transformations require high levels of cognitive engagement. Although flipped learning has been widely implemented to promote active learning, its effectiveness largely depends on the quality of instructional design and pedagogical support provided during in-class activities. This study investigates how metacognitive scaffolding can be intentionally designed and embedded within flipped learning to enhance students’ visual–spatial reasoning. An explanatory sequential mixed-methods design was employed in secondary geometry instruction involving 62 students assigned to experimental and control groups. Quantitative data were collected through pre- and post-tests of visual–spatial reasoning, while qualitative data were obtained from classroom observations and semi-structured teacher interviews. The results indicate that students who experienced metacognitive scaffolding within a flipped learning environment demonstrated significantly greater gains in visual–spatial reasoning than those in a conventional flipped classroom, with a large effect size. Qualitative findings further reveal that scaffolding prompts supported students’ planning, monitoring, and reflective evaluation during problem-solving activities. Overall, the findings suggest that flipped learning environments become more cognitively productive when structured metacognitive scaffolding is deliberately incorporated into the learning design.

papers.title: Knowledge-guided machine learning deciphers spatiotemporal dynamics in chemical reactor systems
papers.abstract: Characterizing the spatiotemporal dynamics of complex chemical reactors, especially localized engineering-critical points or regions, remains challenging in process engineering. Although data-driven methods offer computational advantages, the incorporation of domain-specific physical knowledge can further enhance their predictive performance. Here, we present a physics-informed machine learning framework that systematically embeds coking mechanisms and heat transfer principles into neural network architecture and training constraints. Using a coke-accumulating cracking reactor as a prototypical case, the proposed approach reproduces the spatiotemporal distributions of key operational parameters obtained from conventional simulations with high fidelity and achieves a 105-fold computational acceleration. Crucially, the incorporation of mechanistic knowledge enhances prediction fidelity for critical safety indicators, particularly the maximum external wall temperature (error < 0.5%), enabling precise identification of optimal decoking intervals. This paradigm bridges data efficiency with domain-informed modeling, providing a useful reference for developing real-time monitoring and optimization models for complex industrial systems. A physics-informed neural network embeds coking and heat transfer knowledge via an output integration layer and region-weighted loss to predict reactor spatiotemporal fields; it matches conventional simulation results, improves peak wall temperature accuracy, and runs about five orders of magnitude faster than conventional simulations.

papers.title: Multifidelity Dust Erosion Analysis of Mars Entry Vehicles
papers.abstract: This paper presents a multifidelity approach for estimating dust particle impact effects on the surface of planetary entry vehicles at hypersonic speeds. The multifidelity model used a cokriging approach combining a low-fidelity correlation with a correction factor from high-fidelity solutions. This multifidelity model allows efficient and accurate exploration of spacecraft design space to aid in thermal protection system (TPS) optimization in the presence of dust erosion and enables future computationally efficient uncertainty quantification to help minimize TPS sizing margins. Two sample problems demonstrate the approach: the ExoMars Schiaparelli lander and a hypersonic inflatable aerodynamic decelerator (HIAD) entry vehicle design space. Multifidelity models for the ExoMars and HIAD cases predicted independent high-fidelity test points with 1.83% mean and 5.05% maximum error for ExoMars and 3.84% mean and 11.35% maximum error for HIAD. Once created, the cost of evaluating the multifidelity models was approximately five orders of magnitude lower than one high-fidelity CFD solution. The converged ExoMars multifidelity model was evaluated along the ExoMars Schiaparelli entry trajectory and compared to literature. The HIAD model was applied to a set of entry trajectories to demonstrate the effectiveness of the model for candidate trajectory exploration.

papers.title: Long-horizon embodied manipulation: a survey of methods, trends, and challenges
papers.abstract: Abstract Long-horizon embodied manipulation requires robots to translate abstract goals into extended sequences of reliable physical interactions under partial observability, contact dynamics, sparse feedback, and embodiment constraints. Its difficulty arises not merely from horizon length, but from maintaining semantic dependencies, physical feasibility, task progress, and recoverability across interdependent object-state transformations. This survey systematically reviews the methods, trends, and challenges of this field. We formalize long-horizon embodied manipulation across primitive-action, skill, interaction-event, and semantic-goal horizons, and organize existing methods around three coupled bottlenecks: task structuring, grounded interaction, and progress and adaptation. Accordingly, we examine language- and vision-language-based decomposition, hierarchical reinforcement learning, skill composition, action chunking, sequence and diffusion planning, world models, affordance grounding, progress and reward modeling, memory, replanning, and self-correction. Our analysis reveals a transition from open-loop, model-specific solutions toward hierarchical, affordance-aware, progress-sensitive, and closed-loop systems that coordinate reasoning and control. We further review embodied and simulation benchmarks, arguing that binary success obscures partial completion, error propagation, recovery cost, and horizon-dependent degradation. Finally, we identify open challenges in subgoal reachability, planner-controller alignment, irreversible failure, transferable progress supervision, real-time adaptation, cross-embodiment generalization, sim-to-real reliability, and scalable evaluation, providing a unified foundation for developing dependable robots capable of sustained manipulation in complex environments.

papers.title: State-triggered cooperative mandatory merging at temporary lane closures in mixed traffic flow
papers.abstract: Cooperation can create space at a temporary lane closure, but unnecessary intervention can increase traffic disturbance and fuel use. We develop ECO, a state-triggered strategy that links selective gap creation to mandatory merge execution. Initial target-lane density, remaining distance and controllable-neighbor availability govern activation. Longitudinal model predictive control shapes the gap, while predictive admission, lateral tracking and bounded safety filtering govern execution. Paired simulations assume that all vehicles, including those with nominal human-driving behavior, permit final safety intervention. Across 20 conditions with nonzero target-lane connected and automated vehicle penetration, ECO reduces fuel intensity by 0.80%–7.20% relative to the specified continuous-cooperation controller and completes all 500 main runs. With identical controller settings, activation gating reduces fuel intensity by 1.22%–5.37% at low density and has no effect at the tested higher densities. In a 57-vehicle queue, ECO completes 88.33% of merges versus 66.67% for passive merging, at slightly higher full-horizon fuel use and delay. These results identify a conditional service benefit of cooperation and distinguish it from the operating savings obtained by suppressing unnecessary gap creation.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence in 3D bioprinting: From predictive modeling to autonomous biofabrication
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional bioprinting is shifting from empirically tuned fabrication toward workflows that integrate quantitative data on materials, printing, structure, and biology. This review summarizes how artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning are being used across these areas, with particular attention to studies that include experimental validation. We first discuss conventional measurements such as rheology, filament formation, shape fidelity, and biological assays because these measurements define the inputs and labels used by AI models. We then examine how data from materials, processes, structures, and biology can be linked within the same experiment. Representative studies are compared with respect to the models used, the amount and type of data, validation methods, and whether model outputs were tested in new experiments. Current evidence is strongest for printability prediction, structural quality assessment, and image-based monitoring, while several studies have also demonstrated cell-viability prediction, parameter optimization, transfer learning, Bayesian optimization, and closed-loop correction. We also discuss inverse design, active learning, uncertainty-aware optimization, physics-informed learning, and biological feedback as approaches to reducing the experimental burden. Finally, we use a five-level maturity framework to distinguish AI-assisted analysis, AI-driven recommendations, adaptive control, and autonomous biofabrication. AI is increasingly influencing experimental planning and process control, but fully integrated autonomous workflows remain uncommon. Further progress will depend on validation across materials and platforms, longer-term biological readouts, traceable data, and the reliable integration of experimental feedback.

papers.title: CROWN-UAV: world-model-based planning for risk-aware and auditable UAV navigation
papers.abstract: Autonomous UAV navigation in cluttered warehouses requires anticipation of dynamic and occluded hazards, explicit risk attribution, and recovery-aware action selection. CROWN-UAV integrates an object-centric encoder, a retrained action-conditioned dual world model, stochastic future hypotheses, a calibrated structured risk graph, candidate-level runtime filtering, discrete receding-horizon planning, and planner-grounded audit traces. A frozen, leakage-controlled revision campaign evaluated five implementations on 120 paired NVIDIA Isaac Sim 5.1.0 PhysX cases per method across three warehouse layouts, four hazard families, five disturbance conditions, and two independent scenario seeds. CROWN-Full achieved 59.2% success (95% CI 50.2–67.5%), identical to Greedy and slightly below MPPI (60.8%). Relative to Greedy, CROWN reduced near collisions from 51.7% to 30.8% (paired difference − 20.8% points, Holm-adjusted p = 0.00346) and increased mean minimum clearance by 0.241 m (adjusted p = 5.40e-9), while successful paths were 2.50 m longer and completion was 3.90 s slower on 53 jointly successful cases. At 4.5 s, the DualWorldModel improved UAV ADE (0.313 versus 1.314 m) and occupancy IoU (0.527 versus 0.392) relative to constant velocity, but object ADE was worse (0.772 versus 0.547 m). Full-loop p95 latency was 101.95 ms, with 150/15,170 deadline misses. The evidence supports an implementation-specific proximity-safety trade-off and auditable decision records, not higher task completion, universal predictor superiority, formal safety, or human-validated explainability.

papers.title: BASIL: Bayesian Adaptive State Imagination and Learning with Live Telemetry Halting and In-Context Rule Induction
papers.abstract: Planning in unfamiliar environments requires an agent to infer governing rules, decide whether additional computation is useful, and determine when to stop searching. We study these questions in Multiverse, a procedural benchmark of two-player connection games with disjoint training, validation, and test rule families. A baseline pre-search value-of-computation predictor has zero-valued labels on 73% of sampled states and a held-out correlation of −0.004 with reference planning gain. BASIL combines three mechanisms: a rule-conditioned world model with boundary-aware convolutions, a discrete board-state carrier and a symbolic tactical horizon; Live Telemetry Halting (LTH), which predicts a completed-search action-value gap from intermediate search telemetry; and Bayesian Hypothesis Filtration (BHF), which maintains a posterior over finite rule hypotheses across episodes. In a three-seed validation study, full search scores 0.958 against a greedy opponent and 0.771 against a 100-rollout simulator-search opponent, compared with 0.549 and 0.424 for the fast policy. Against the latter opponent, LTH scores 0.646 using 8.2 rather than 33.9 model expansions per move. On the held-out test split, full-search scores are 0.938 and 0.722, respectively. In six-episode hidden-rule matches, posterior entropy falls from 6.49 to 1.69 bits and posterior-sampled search reaches a score of 0.757 in the final two episodes. These results support adaptive planning within the specified rule grammar, while comparisons with heuristic stopping rules and the cost of symbolic operations delimit the conclusions. Keywords—Model-based reinforcement learning; Adaptive computation; Monte Carlo tree search; Optimal stopping; Bayesian rule induction; World models

papers.title: Biocompatibility evaluation of a dECM-enriched alginate-gelatin bioink-derived hydrogel for vascular tissue engineering.
papers.abstract: Decellularized extracellular matrix (dECM)-based biomaterials have gained increasing attention in vascular tissue engineering due to their bioactivity and tissue-specific composition. In this study, we evaluated the in vitro cellular response and short-term in vivo biocompatibility of a dECM-enriched alginate-gelatin bioink-derived hydrogel previously developed for bioprinting applications. Hydrogel constructs containing porcine aorta-derived dECM or without dECM (control) were assessed using human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs), human aortic smooth muscle cells (HASMCs), a whole-blood clotting assay, and subcutaneous implantation in rats. HUVECs cultured on the dECM-containing hydrogel showed approximately two- to four-fold higher metabolic activity than those cultured on the control formulation, with a significant formulation × time interaction, whereas HASMCs showed an overall lower metabolic activity in the dECM-containing formulation without a significant formulation × time interaction. Whole-blood clotting kinetics did not significantly differ between formulations in this preliminary assay. Following subcutaneous implantation, both formulations exhibited an early peri-implant host response characterized by serous fluid accumulation and macrophage presence, with collagen-containing peri-implant tissue observed during the 2-week study period. Within the limited animal sample, no statistically significant formulation-dependent differences were detected in the quantified histological or immunofluorescence endpoints. Overall, these findings provide preliminary evidence supporting the short-term biological compatibility of the dECM-enriched hydrogel and warrant further evaluation in bioprinted constructs and physiologically relevant vascular models.

papers.title: Monoflange Versus Multiflange: Custom-Made Acetabular Implants in Revision Total Hip Arthroplasty.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Severe acetabular bone loss remains a major challenge in hip reconstruction. Custom-made acetabular components (CMACs) represent a valuable treatment option, with monoflange designs potentially offering advantages over multiflange constructs by reducing implant size and soft-tissue exposure while maintaining mechanical stability. METHODS: This retrospective, single-center study analyzed 154 CMACs (101 monoflange and 53 multiflange) and assessed clinical outcomes (Oxford Hip Score), radiographic findings, complications, implant survival, and revision procedures. The mean follow-up was 37.0 months (range, 6.2 to 168.2), with longer follow-up for multiflange than monoflange constructs (55.5 versus 27.3 months; P = 0.011). RESULTS: Monoflange constructs showed shorter hospital stays (P = 0.030), reduced blood losses (P < 0.001), and shorter operative times (P = 0.006). Both groups improved in Oxford Hip Score (OHS), with higher postoperative scores for monoflange constructs (P = 0.010), although adjusted mean change in OHS did not differ (P = 0.566). Periprosthetic joint infection rates were higher for multiflange constructs (18.9 versus 6.9%; P = 0.034). Complete osseointegration was achieved in 93.1% of monoflange and 67.9% of multiflange constructs (P < 0.001). Horizontal center of rotation restoration was comparable (0.9 ± 5.0 versus 2.0 ± 5.7 mm; P = 0.236), whereas monoflange constructs showed less cranialization (3.5 ± 4.5 mm versus 7.6 ± 5.6 mm; P < 0.001). Multiflange design was associated with a higher risk of implant removal (odds ratio = 4.42; P = 0.007). CONCLUSION: Monoflange CMACs demonstrated favorable clinical and radiographic outcomes and, after adjustment for patient factors, a significantly lower risk of implant removal than multiflange constructs. As implant design and era are confounded in this cohort, these findings should be interpreted as associations and require confirmation in prospective series.

papers.title: DreamFAR: Real-Time and Long-Horizon Interaction with Diverse Objects
papers.abstract: World models have shown great potential in serving as a simulator for robot manipulation. However, existing models are either fit to a single environment or lack ability to simulate long-horizon contact-rich events. We present DreamFAR, a world model whose dynamics model is trained from scratch on a large robot-native teleoperation dataset, with no internet-video pretraining. We present an architecture and learning recipe designed for training on robot-native data. DreamFAR is significantly smaller than the high-performance video generation models, yet shows better understanding of contact and causality, and runs 10 FPS on a commercial GPU. Experimentally, DreamFAR significantly outperforms existing models in predicting the long-horizon future. We further demonstrate various applications where DreamFAR can be used, including policy evaluation and mixed-data co-training. Project page: https://www.yimingdou.com/DreamFAR/

papers.title: ThermLeT: Transformer-based Temperature Prediction for 2.5D Chiplet Architecture
papers.abstract: The drive toward heterogeneous 2.5D chiplet packages promises unmatched performance and customization, yet the resulting density amplifies thermal challenges. To facilitate rapid design space exploration, we present ThermLeT, a multimodal transformer-based, scale invariant surrogate that integrates power density maps, spatial coordinate embeddings, material properties and heat transfer rate to predict steady state temperature in 13 ms, about four orders of magnitude faster than conventional finite element solvers such as ANSYS. To train the transformer model, we also create a dataset of 6,221 chiplet layouts perturbed from three representative architectures. On a 150 sample test set, ThermLeT achieves an RMSE of 3.16°C and an MAE of 2.24°C, improving accuracy by 35% over ThermEDGe and by 71% over HotSpot, while running approximately 6x and 11x lower inference latencies respectively. Ablation studies confirm robust generalization to unseen floorplans. Code and dataset available at https://github.com/MicroSystemsDesignLab/ThermLeT

papers.title: Higher-Order Interaction Reconstruction via Integral Physics-Informed Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Reconstructing higher-order interactions is a fundamental challenge in complex networked systems, with applications in ecological, social, and biological networks. This inverse problem is inherently difficult due to the combinatorial complexity of higher-order structures, the strong nonlinearity of the underlying dynamics, and the prevalence of noisy and sparse observations. In this article, we propose a novel integral physics-informed neural network (IntegralPINN) framework for higher-order interaction reconstruction. Instead of { penalizing derivative-based physics residuals,} we adopt an integral formulation over temporal intervals, which naturally suppresses high-frequency noise and mitigates derivative-induced instability. We further introduce a continuous parameterization of interaction tensors, enabling tractable identification of higher-order structures via gradient-based optimization. We provide theoretical analysis establishing a noise-robust error bound that is independent of derivative amplification when the integration window satisfies an excitation condition. Extensive experiments on ecological dynamics, social contagion, and neuronal synchronization systems demonstrate that IntegralPINN achieves accurate and robust reconstruction under noisy and sparse observations, outperforming state-of-the-art approaches.

papers.title: Physics-informed neural networks for spacecraft trajectory optimization with exact boundary conditions
papers.abstract: We use neural networks to optimize trajectories by modeling the position as a function of time and minimizing the thrust with respect to the network parameters. This corresponds to an unsupervised training procedure in which physical laws are incorporated directly into the optimization objective. In standard physics-informed neural networks, initial and terminal states are enforced through additional weighted loss terms, resulting in a multi-objective optimization problem that is highly sensitive to the choice of loss weights and can lead to poor convergence and reduced accuracy. To address this challenge, we construct a simple transformation, exploiting the mathematical structure of trajectory optimization problems, to enforce boundary conditions exactly a-priori. This transformation can be interpreted as a reparameterization of the solution space that embeds the boundary conditions directly into the function. This converts the original constrained optimization problem into an unconstrained one over admissible trajectories. I.e. the transformation eliminates the boundary condition penalty terms and reduces the problem to a single-objective optimization. Crucially, trajectory optimization comes with a low-dimensional boundary, which allows particularly simple and stable constructions of distance functions compared to general domains in partial differential equations. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed approach meaningfully improves convergence behavior and solution accuracy.

papers.title: From Human Videos to Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation Data: Confidence-Guided RL Refinement of Video Priors
papers.abstract: Collecting demonstrations for bimanual dexterous manipulation is costly, motivating the use of human videos as a source of robot training data. However, uncertainty in video-derived motion estimates and differences between human and robot embodiments make direct motion transfer challenging. In this work, we introduce PriDex, a framework that transforms human-video Priors into executable robot Dexterous manipulation demonstrations through reinforcement learning in simulation. PriDex preserves task-relevant interaction structure while allowing embodiment-specific behavior to be regenerated for the robot. Human-object interactions provide affordance cues for selecting task-relevant, robot-specific grasps from geometry-based candidates. For motion refinement, object trajectories provide a task-level reference, while relative bimanual wrist trajectories offer complementary guidance for coordinated motion. Since object-motion estimates can become unreliable under occlusion or visual ambiguity, PriDex uses object-motion confidence to adaptively balance these two priors, emphasizing object-level guidance when confidence is high and increasing the contribution of wrist-level guidance as confidence decreases. Reinforcement learning refines these video-derived priors under the robot's kinematic and physical constraints, and the resulting policies are rolled out to generate robot demonstrations for training a vision-based diffusion policy. We evaluate PriDex on four bimanual dexterous manipulation tasks, including pouring, sweeping into a dustpan, bottle-cap unscrewing, and plate cleaning, assessing both simulation-based robot data generation and downstream visuomotor policy learning.

papers.title: World-Grounded Reinforcement Learning for Pollution-Aware Bird Movement Modeling Using a Multi-Instance DQN Framework
papers.abstract: Birds are modeled as environmentally sensitive agents whose movement reflects real-world air quality conditions, where AQI serves as a measurable world feedback signal representing pollution-driven consequences. Instead of relying on human preference or synthetic rewards, the system uses environmental outcomes as the primary training signal, enabling policy learning grounded in ecological impact. We propose a multi-instance reinforcement learning simulation in which agents navigate a 2D grid representation of India integrated with a precomputed AQI matrix and geographic state boundaries. The framework combines bird call metadata from the Xeno-canto dataset, spatial discretization, and real environmental data to learn adaptive navigation strategies under pollution constraints. To ensure scalability and efficiency, repeated real-time API queries are replaced by a structured AQI mapping that enables fast lookup during training and execution. Multiple baselines, including Monte Carlo, Q-Learning, and Value Iteration, are evaluated for comparison. Deep Q-Network demonstrates stronger stability, adaptability, and cumulative performance across varying environmental conditions, establishing a scalable foundation for world-feedback driven ecological decision modeling.

papers.title: WM-Quant: Rollout-Aware Post-Training Quantization for JEPA-Style World Models
papers.abstract: We present WM-Quant, to our knowledge, the first post-training quantization (PTQ) framework designed specifically for JEPA-style world models. Although world models typically feature relatively few parameters, action planning algorithms often require thousands of inferences, which can quickly become computationally expensive. PTQ is a natural way to reduce this cost. However, we show that in world models using autoregressive model predictive control (MPC) rollouts, quantization error can compound with each predictor step, resulting in action rankings from the quantized model becoming near-random. WM-Quant addresses this with three components that build on existing PTQ methods: early-encoder precision, control-path preservation, and rollout-aware scaling. Early-encoder precision protects accurate latent state and goal information to mitigate long-term error propagation. Control-path preservation allows the world model predictor to distinguish between fine-grained actions, significantly improving action rankings and execution. Rollout-aware scaling jointly calibrates encoder and per-step predictor activation ranges with respect to an entire rollout rather than a single prediction, reducing the cumulative rollout error. Across multiple world models, environments, and PTQ methods, WM-Quant substantially improves planning success at low bit-widths, approaching full-precision performance at W4A4.

papers.title: Can a World Model Predict a Deepfake Video? A Consistency Margin Prior for Deepfake Detection
papers.abstract: Deepfake detectors often perform well on the dataset they are trained on, but their performance drops when tested on videos from different datasets. In this paper, we study whether a predictive video model can provide a signal that generalizes better across datasets. Instead of relying only on generator-specific artifacts, as many existing detectors do, we use a model trained to predict natural video and measure the difference between what it predicts and what it observes in a video. Using V-JEPA 2.1, we keep the encoder frozen and adapt the predictor using rank-16 LoRA. We define the difference between the predictor output and the frozen encoder target as the prediction residual. We hypothesize that manipulated clips produce, on average, larger prediction residuals than authentic clips, and use this as our consistency-margin prior. We process these residuals using a lightweight Latent Consistency Head (LCH), which separates residual magnitude from direction for training and classification. To test whether the direction of the consistency margin affects cross-dataset generalization, we compare standard and reversed margin objectives while keeping the remaining training setup fixed. We match the two settings on FF++ validation performance before evaluating them on unseen data. The reversed-margin setting exhibits a larger cross dataset generalization gap on average, providing evidence that the direction of the consistency margin affects cross-dataset transfer. Our complete model adds only 8.25M trainable parameters, which is 2.47% of the total 334M parameters. Trained only on FF++, it achieves an AUC of 90.5 on Celeb-DFv2 and performs well across several other cross-dataset benchmarks. Our ablations show that separating residual magnitude from direction, reducing dataset-specific variation, and using a low-rank projection improve cross-dataset generalization in our experiments.
