papers.title: Better Calibrated, Better Planned: Uncertainty-Aware Multi-ASV Informative Path Planning for Oil Spill Monitoring
papers.abstract: Monitoring oil spills with fleets of Autonomous Surface Vehicles (ASVs) requires mapping a heterogeneous pollutant field from sparse, noisy measurements under tight time and energy budgets. Informative Path Planning (IPP) addresses this problem by coupling a reconstruction model, which infers the field and its uncertainty, with a planner that decides where to sample next. Prior work has focused on planning strategies and has largely relied on Gaussian Processes (GPs), leaving the calibration of the model's uncertainty underexplored. We study how uncertainty calibration conditions multi-vehicle IPP with a fleet of ASVs that coordinates online through a shared uncertainty map. We introduce Evidential Deep Learning (EDL) as an uncertainty-calibrated information model. We benchmark EDL, Monte Carlo Dropout and Deep Ensembles against a GP in closed loop with five planners on physics-based oil spill simulations. Across 60 maps, the choice of model dominates the outcome, explaining 80\% of the variance of the final reconstruction error, against 1\% for the planner among the deep models. EDL achieves the lowest error and the highest IoU under every planner, is the best calibrated model and runs at 3.9 ms per step. With 50 cells per vehicle it reconstructs the spill better than MC Dropout and Deep Ensembles with 150. Deep Ensembles become more confident as their error grows, whereas EDL is unaffected. Robustness of the information model to the data its own planner collects is therefore a requirement of uncertainty-aware IPP.

papers.title: Bookkeeping Is Not Judgement: EJBench, an Engineering Judgement Benchmark Built from a Conjugate Heat Transfer Design Campaign
papers.abstract: We introduce EJBench, a benchmark of engineering judgement: whether a model can predict how a design behaves at new conditions from a few earlier results, and decide on it. Unlike engineering benchmarks that test whether an agent can operate simulation or CAD software, EJBench is software-agnostic and asks what an engineer would conclude without running a simulation. Its tasks come from a conjugate heat transfer design campaign for battery cold plates, in three families: matching unlabelled test results to their operating points, choosing which stored runs to reveal before signing off a design, and ranking new duties by peak cell temperature. Every answer is taken from a converged simulation, not from an LLM judge. The best of ten frontier models, GPT-6 Astra, scores 0.71, and models state almost the same confidence on tasks they get wrong as on tasks they get right. We also post-train Qwen3.5-9B with LoRA and reinforcement learning, rewarded by the share of answer criteria the simulation results confirm; on the held-out test split its score rises from 0.071 to 0.106. We release the train, validation and test splits, the evaluation harness and the leaderboard.

papers.title: Accuracy of Cone-beam Computed Tomography in Determining Implant Length and Diameter: A Comparative Clinical Evaluation
papers.abstract: Abstract Background: Accurate preoperative assessment of implant dimensions is a critical determinant of success in dental implant therapy. Precise estimation of implant length and diameter helps avoid complications such as cortical plate perforation, inferior alveolar nerve injury, and inadequate primary stability. Cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) has become an important imaging modality in implant dentistry because it provides three-dimensional visualization with relatively low radiation exposure compared to conventional computed tomography. Aim: The study aimed to evaluate the accuracy of CBCT in determining implant length and diameter by comparing radiographic measurements with actual implant dimensions used during surgery. Study Design and Setting: This was a prospective, comparative clinical study conducted in a dental teaching hospital. Subjects and Methods: Patients requiring dental implant placement were included in the study. Preoperative CBCT scans were obtained, and measurements of proposed implant length and diameter were recorded using dedicated CBCT software. During implant placement, the actual implant length and diameter used were documented. Radiographic measurements obtained from CBCT were then compared with the clinical implant dimensions. Results: CBCT measurements showed a high degree of agreement with the actual implant length and diameter used during surgery. Minor discrepancies were observed, but these differences were within clinically acceptable limits. CBCT demonstrated high accuracy in preoperative assessment of implant dimensions. Conclusion: CBCT is a reliable and accurate imaging modality for determining implant length and diameter. Its use in preoperative planning can enhance surgical safety and improve the clinical outcomes in dental implant therapy.

papers.title: Short-Fiber-Reinforced Thermoplastic Composites for Fused Deposition Modeling: Material Systems, Process Parameter Control, and Performance Optimization
papers.abstract: Short-fiber-reinforced thermoplastic composites combine the processability of polymer matrices with the high strength and stiffness of short fibers, offering an effective route to enhance the performance of parts fabricated by Fused Deposition Modeling (FDM). This review summarizes recent advances in short carbon fiber-, short glass fiber-, and short basalt fiber-reinforced thermoplastic composites based on PLA, ABS, PA, and PEEK matrices. The effects of fiber type, content, length retention, orientation, and interfacial bonding on reinforcement behavior are discussed. The roles of key FDM parameters, including nozzle temperature, printing speed, layer thickness, infill density, and raster angle, in governing melt flow, fiber orientation, interlayer bonding, porosity, crystallization, and mechanical performance are systematically reviewed. Numerical approaches, including computational fluid dynamics (CFD), smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH), the discrete element method (DEM), finite element analysis (FEA), and multiscale homogenization, are summarized for process simulation and microstructure–property prediction, together with optimization strategies based on design of experiments, response surface methodology, and multi-objective optimization. Finally, emerging data-driven methods, including machine learning, Bayesian optimization, and digital twins, are discussed for performance prediction, inverse process design, and closed-loop manufacturing. Collectively, these simulation and optimization approaches provide a practical framework for reducing experimental trial and error, identifying robust printing windows, anticipating fiber- and porosity-related defects, and balancing mechanical performance against manufacturing efficiency. They also support physics-informed, data-driven process design and more reliable scale-up of short-fiber-reinforced FDM materials.

papers.title: Progress and Current Status of Biodegradable Metallic Implants: Mini-Review
papers.abstract: Biodegradable metallic implants have emerged as promising alternatives to conventional permanent implants by eliminating the need for secondary removal surgery while providing temporary mechanical support during tissue healing. This review presents recent advances in biodegradable metallic biomaterials, with particular emphasis on magnesium-, zinc-, and iron-based alloys. The mechanical properties, degradation behaviour, biocompatibility, and clinical potential of these materials are reviewed, highlighting their advantages and current limitations. Recent developments in alloy design, surface engineering, additive manufacturing, nanotechnology, and friction stir processing are discussed as approaches to control degradation while supporting mechanical integrity, osseointegration, and antibacterial performance. The review further examines multifunctional surface coatings and emerging smart implant technologies designed to reduce implant-associated infections and enhance tissue regeneration. The review also distinguishes material-level findings from device-specific clinical evidence across magnesium-, zinc-, and iron-based implants.

papers.title: Graph foundation models for intelligent monitoring and control of renewable energy networks
papers.abstract: The rapid expansion of renewable energy resources has transformed modern power systems into highly interconnected and dynamic networks that require intelligent monitoring and adaptive control. Existing graph-based approaches mainly learn structural relationships from historical data and do not explicitly respect the electrical laws of the network. This paper proposes a physics-informed graph foundation model (PI-GFM) coupled with a digital twin (DT) for monitoring and control of renewable energy networks. PI-GFM is an impedance-aware graph encoder that is pre-trained in a self-supervised manner on pooled heterogeneous network data and then adapted through task heads for fault classification, bus-voltage estimation and one-hour-ahead DT forecasting. Electrical knowledge enters as soft penalties on nodal active and reactive power balance and on the linearised (LinDistFlow) branch voltage drop; the full nonlinear AC power flow is not enforced, and this scope is stated explicitly. The DT synchronises a latent network state over a four-hour window through a learned fusion, under explicitly defined operating limits, and its voltage estimates drive a reactive-power support controller. The framework is evaluated on a fully specified simulation of the IEEE 33-bus feeder with photovoltaic, wind and battery resources, solved with AC power flow and subjected to inverter faults, high-impedance line faults, voltage-instability events and reconfigurations, using chronological splits, 5 random seeds and DNN, LSTM, GCN, GAT and GraphSAGE baselines. On the unseen test season, PI-GFM attains a bus-voltage MAE of 3.31 × 10 −3 p.u., 17% lower than the best baseline (3.96 × 10 −3 p.u.), and a DT synchronisation accuracy of 84.9% of bus-hours within 0.005 p.u. (best baseline 75.9%). Its four-class accuracy is 96.39% (best baseline 97.12%), with a fault-detection false-alarm rate of 1.29%. Used as controller input, it keeps all buses within 0.95–1.05 p.u. in 88.2% of test hours, against 85.8% without control and 96.9% with perfect state knowledge. The ablation shows that both the physics terms and the DT reduce the estimation error, and pre-training improves low-label performance. The results are obtained on simulated data, on one feeder family, on a single CPU platform.

papers.title: A lightweight coastal digital twin for real-time flood and impact forecasting using ensemble data assimilation and machine learning
papers.abstract: Coastal flood forecasting systems increasingly need to provide not only point-based water-level predictions, but also probabilistic flood extents and impact-relevant information at operational time scales. This study presents a prototype coastal digital twin framework for real-time flood and impact forecasting along the U.S. East and Gulf Coasts. The framework integrates four coupled components: a machine-learning (ML) storm surge forecasting module, an ensemble Kalman filter (EnKF) for probabilistic uncertainty updating, a rapid inundation mapping method based on topographically constrained connectivity filtering, and a first-order impact layer based on population exposure and depth-damage relationships. The framework is evaluated at six tide-gauge stations representing four U.S. coastal regimes. Four ML models are trained using multi-decadal hourly water-level and meteorological records to predict storm-surge levels across multiple lead times, and a meta-stack ensemble is used to combine model outputs while preserving computational efficiency. The EnKF provides probabilistic surge forecasts and improves predictions during coastal extremes. The storm-tide forecasts, obtained by adding surge forecasts and astronomical tide predictions, are then propagated through the inundation and impact modules to generate forecast-conditioned flood and consequence ranges. Results show that the meta-stack provides robust deterministic forecasts across stations, while the data-assimilation layer improves extreme-event accuracy and interval coverage. Overall, the framework establishes a flexible and computationally efficient prototype for real-time coastal flood digital twins, linking observations, probabilistic forecasts, inundation, and first-order impacts within a single operational workflow.

papers.title: Comparative Analysis of Optimization Algorithms for PID Controller Tuning in Electric Vehicles
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Electric vehicles (EVs) are quickly becoming a leading eco‐friendly alternative in today's transportation sector, prioritizing energy efficiency, stability, and safety. One of the most critical aspects of maximizing EV performance is fine‐tuning control systems, especially proportional‐integral‐derivative (PID) controllers. These controllers play a vital role in managing vehicle dynamics, powertrain efficiency, and overall stability. This paper offers a comparative simulation study of optimization algorithms for tuning PID controllers in EV systems. Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Genetic Algorithm (GA), Simulated Annealing (SA), and Bayesian Optimization (BO) are compared under the same conditions to ensure a fair comparison. The algorithms are compared in terms of transient response characteristics, convergence properties, computational requirements, and a normalized performance index. The outcome of the study shows that the use of optimization algorithms in PID tuning performs better compared to the manual method. Although Bayesian Optimization performs well with fewer evaluations, Particle Swarm Optimization has a better balance of convergence speed and control performance, making it more desirable for real‐time applications. Quantitatively, optimization‐based tuning raised the operating efficiency from 79.9% for manually tuned PID gains to 94.34% (PSO), 95.82% (GA), 95.98% (SA), and 96.78% (BO), while Bayesian Optimization reached its result in only 30 function evaluations and PSO required the lowest average execution time (4.02 s) among the four algorithms, evidencing a clear efficiency‐versus‐computational‐cost trade‐off across methods. Future studies will involve real‐time implementation and hardware‐in‐the‐loop simulation.

papers.title: Synergetic Model Predictive Decoupled Active and Reactive Power Control for Single-Phase SAPF System Using Nine-Level Modified Packed E-Cell (MPEC9) Inverter
papers.abstract: The growing use of nonlinear loads in industrial and residential applications degrades power quality through harmonic distortion and increased reactive power demand. Shunt active power filters (SAPFs) mitigate these disturbances at the point of common coupling (PCC). This paper proposes a modified packed E-cell nine-level inverter (MPEC9) for a single-phase SAPF. A Synergetic Model Predictive Decoupled Powers Control (DPC-SMPC) strategy combines synergetic control theory with model predictive control to regulate grid-side active and reactive powers while maintaining balanced DC-bus capacitor voltages. In this algorithm, the defined macro-variable is predicted to determine the optimal voltage vector associated with the active and reactive power references in a single evaluation. Subsequently, the capacitor voltages are predicted for all admissible switching states and incorporated into the cost function alongside the optimal voltage vector. The proposed DPC-SMPC achieves the control objectives with reduced computational burden. The proposed inverter and control strategy are evaluated through processor-in-the-loop (PIL) co-simulation. Comparative results against the DPC-MPC strategy demonstrate improved performance across the evaluated criteria and lower computational requirements, supporting the effectiveness of the proposed approach for power quality improvement and coordinated power regulation in the investigated single-phase SAPF system under evaluation.

papers.title: Active learning–based efficient seismic response prediction of base-isolated structures using linear time-history analyses
papers.abstract: Deep learning models for seismic response prediction often require extensive datasets generated through repeated time-history analyses. This study investigates uncertainty-driven active learning for training a long short-term memory model to predict complete roof-displacement histories of base-isolated structures. A numerical database comprising 1000 linear time-history simulations was developed using recorded earthquake ground motions and varying isolation parameters. Monte Carlo dropout-based uncertainty acquisition was compared with random and diversity-based sampling across 10 matched repetitions and labeled-sample budgets ranging from 100 to 300. Performance was evaluated on ground-motion records withheld from model development. The results reveal substantial variability and nonmonotonic learning behavior. Uncertainty-based acquisition did not consistently outperform the alternative strategies, and negative mean R 2 values indicated difficulties in generalizing to unseen ground-motion records. Nevertheless, Monte Carlo dropout uncertainty scores exhibited a strong positive correlation with actual prediction errors (Spearman ρ = 0.8697). These findings highlight both the diagnostic value and the limitations of uncertainty-driven sample acquisition for seismic response-history prediction.

papers.title: DUAL-HORIZON PROACTIVE PHYSICS-INFORMED MODEL-BASED REINFORCEMENT LEARNING CONTROL FOR 10 MW OFFSHORE PMSG WIND ENERGY SYSTEMS UNDER LVRT FAULTS AND TURBULENT WIND
papers.abstract: Multi-megawatt offshore wind energy conversion systems based on surfacemounted Permanent Magnet Synchronous Generators (PMSGs) face severe operational challenges in maintaining DC-link voltage stability and power quality under simultaneous sub-cycle grid faults and high-turbulence wind regimes.Conventional model-free Reinforcement Learning (RL) controllers rely on reactive error-driven updates, often resulting in delayed transient responses, high-frequency control chatter, and frequent hardware brake chopper activation during Low-Voltage Ride-Through (LVRT) events.Conversely, purely data-driven Model-Based RL (MBRL) approaches require extensive fault-state training datasets and suffer from multi-step prediction drift.To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes a Dual-Horizon Proactive Physics-Informed Model-Based Reinforcement Learning (PI-MBRL) control architecture for a 10 MW offshore PMSG wind energy system.By embedding analytical DC-link and converter state-space equations directly into the predictive rollout loop, the framework evaluates two decoupled look-ahead horizons: a fast 15 ms electrical horizon for subcycle grid voltage sag detection and pre-emptive active power de-loading, and a slow 300 ms aerodynamic horizon for feedforward turbulent wind power gradient smoothing.

papers.title: A Distributed Predictive Control Approach to Formation Control With Collision Avoidance via Virtual Edge Dynamics
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT In this paper we propose a novel approach to distributed predictive formation control for a network of autonomous vehicles (agents) with collision avoidance. The interaction topology through which neighboring agents exchange information is usually represented by a connected and undirected graph, where the nodes are associated with agents and the edges represent communication links. Since the optimal control problem (OCP) that each agent needs to solve in each model predictive control (MPC) step requires information from the whole network, a standard way of handling this is to use iterative MPC schemes. These schemes require multiple solutions of the OCP in each MPC step, which might render them impractical for real‐time implementation. We propose to consider instead the auxiliary problem of controlling a multi‐agent system (MAS) where the agents are associated not with the nodes but with the edges of the interaction graph. This allows to decouple the individual OCPs and thus avoids the need of multiple solutions in one MPC step. Iteration can however not be avoided completely: agents need to run an iterative steepest descent algorithm with their neighbors in order to recover the physical control inputs from the solutions obtained on the edge system. The iterative steepest descent algorithm is computationally much cheaper than multiple solutions of the OCPs; a comparison with a standard Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) distributed MPC approach in a simulation example suggests that our proposed method speeds up the computation by almost two orders of magnitude. While in this approach it is not possible to include absolute constraints on agents states or inputs in the OCPs, it is possible to consider collision avoidance constraints, which are relative constraints between agents.

papers.title: Adaptive Motion Scaling With Phase‐and‐Gaze Awareness for Laparoscopic Robotic Teleoperation
papers.abstract: Teleoperated surgical robots commonly employ a small fixed motion scaling factor to improve precision and suppress hand tremor. However, in laparoscopic teleoperation, this configuration limits the effective workspace on the slave side and necessitates frequent clutching during large‐range motions, thereby diverting the operator's attention and increasing cognitive workload. To address this, this article proposes a phase‐ and gaze‐aware adaptive motion scaling framework for laparoscopic robotic teleoperation, integrating real‐time surgical phase recognition, fusion of robot kinematics and eye‐tracking features, and personalized parameter tuning based on Bayesian optimization. The inferred phase probabilities and dominance weights are used to suppress unnecessary scaling fluctuations during fine manipulation while preserving responsiveness during coarse manipulation. Eye‐tracking features are used as attention‐related cues and fused with robot kinematics to determine motion scaling online. To validate the proposed framework, personalized optimization experiments and pilot within‐subject comparison studies were conducted with eight nonclinical participants. The results show that, compared with fixed and other adaptive scaling methods, the proposed method can reduce clutching frequency, shorten task completion time, and improve subjective ratings. These results indicate that the proposed framework can provide self‐adaptive and stable motion mapping for laparoscopic robotic teleoperation, offering a transferable strategy for broader robotic teleoperation scenarios.

A qualitative case study approach was employed. papers.title: Deep Learning Solutions to Third-Order ODEs via Physics-Informed Neural Network
papers.abstract: The resolution of third-order ordinary differential equations is crucial in our understanding of complex systems used in scientific and engineering applications. Traditional computational techniques such as the New Iterative Method (NIM) and Adomian Decomposition Method (ADM) provide solutions to third-order ODEs but are limited by high computational cost, efficiency and accuracy. To address these difficulties, we developed and implemented a proposed Physics-Informed Neural Network model to provide a precise solution to third-order ODEs by integrating deep learning with physical laws, and compared its performance with existing methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency. The proposed PINN model is trained utilizing forward propagation to minimize the loss function by incorporating the ODE residuals and initial criteria into the training process, enabling the neural network to learn the governing equation effectively and also uses backpropagation for optimization of the neural network parameters in order to generate a precise solution with minimal error. We test the effectiveness of the model using five(5) third-order ODEs problems and the results showcase that the Proposed PINN framework is superior for approximating third-order ODEs than the NIM and ADM approaches by producing accurate solutions while also maintaining low error values ranging from of 10-7 to 10-10 . Also, the loss curves and computational-time analysis provide evidence of the model's ability to obtain accurate solutions efficiently. These findings demonstrate the potential of the PINN model in producing accurate and efficient solutions, therefore contributing to the application of deep-learning in applied mathematics and scientific computing.

summary_en.motivation: Conventional iterative schemes for third-order ODEs suffer from high cost and limited accuracy.
summary_en.method: A physics-informed neural network is trained by embedding ODE residuals and initial conditions into the loss and optimizing via backpropagation.
summary_en.result: Across five third-order ODE problems the model attains errors of 10^-7 to 10^-10, outperforming NIM and ADM in accuracy and runtime.
summary_en.validation: Performance is assessed on five benchmark ODE problems through error, loss-curve, and computational-time comparisons.

papers.title: Machine learning-driven microstructure prediction and bayesian optimization for nickel-based superalloy hot forging process
papers.abstract: The microstructural evolution of nickel-based superalloys during hot forging is modulated by the complex coupling effects of multiple process parameters, and the corresponding processing-microstructure relationship exhibits prominent nonlinear characteristics. In the present study, a machine learning-based model is developed to predict the microstructure of nickel-based superalloys during hot forging and realize the reverse multi-objective optimization of process parameters. A total of 120 isothermal compression tests were conducted on GH4706 alloy in this work. Deformation temperature, strain rate, and strain within specific ranges were selected as input features, while dynamic recrystallization fraction, grain size standard deviation, and average grain size were defined as output response variables. Four extensively adopted machine learning models were systematically compared, and the Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) model was validated to outperform the others in prediction performance. This paper further quantitatively characterizes the contribution of each process parameter to model prediction. On the basis of the trained GPR model, the optimal hot forging process window for GH4706 alloy is identified as temperature = 1090 – 1140 °C, strain = 1.0 – 1.2, strain rate = 0.003 – 0.042 s⁻¹, which can simultaneously achieve high dynamic recrystallization fraction, refined grain size, and homogeneous microstructure. This work establishes a closed-loop intelligent manufacturing framework integrating "process design-microstructure prediction-parameter optimization", and verifies that GPR, leveraging its advantages in uncertainty quantification, small-sample adaptability, and physical interpretability, can serve as an efficient and reliable data-driven tool for precise microstructure control of nickel-based superalloy forgings.

summary_en.motivation: The coupled influence of multiple forging parameters on microstructural evolution is strongly nonlinear, making efficient prediction and inverse process design difficult.
summary_en.method: Four machine learning models were compared on 120 isothermal compression tests of GH4706, with Gaussian process regression used to predict recrystallization fraction and grain size statistics and to drive Bayesian multi-objective optimization of process parameters.
summary_en.result: GPR outperformed the alternatives and yielded an optimal forging window achieving high recrystallization fraction, refined grains, and microstructural homogeneity.
summary_en.validation: Model performance and the optimized window were assessed against experimental isothermal compression data for GH4706 alloy.

papers.title: The Current State and Development Prospects of Pre-Master’s Training for International Citizens in Russian Technical Universities
papers.abstract: Aim. To consider the current state and prospects for the development of pre-master’s degree training for foreign citizens in technical universities of Russia. To identify and solve didactic, methodological, pedagogical and organizational contradictions, to analyse the level model of individualization of educational programs for the intensification of specialized training of foreign undergraduates of engineering specialties.Methodology. During the study, the author applies a system analysis, a comparative method for the analysis of foreign and domestic experience in teaching foreign citizens. The article substantiates the prospects for the direction of development based on the resolution of the identified contradictions with the use of a competency-based, personal approach and ensuring the continuity of education. The empirical base consists of local regulations, curricula and programs of preparatory faculties of 9 leading technical universities of the Russian Federation. The methods of content analysis of educational programs and generalisation of pedagogical experience in the field of teaching Russian as a foreign language were used.Research implications. This paper systematizes the main existing forms and models of pre-master’s degree training for foreign citizens implemented at Russian universities. A critical gap between pre-university language training (B1) and the actual requirements for scientific communication in engineering disciplines at the master's and postgraduate levels is highlighted. A multi-level model for shaping the educational trajectories of international students at the early stages of their studies is proposed. The theoretical significance of the study lies in clarifying the principles of integrating teaching methods for general engineering disciplines in Russian as a foreign language for applicants with A0 Russian language proficiency. The practical significance lies in the potential use of the results to modernize curricula and reduce student attrition during the transition from pre-university training to master's programs.Conclusions. The current state of pre-master’s training for international students is institutionalised within preparatory faculties / departments and demonstrates steady growth in program evolution. An analysis of existing training programs for international students based on nine technical universities in the Russian Federation, as well as research articles on this issue, revealed a number of systemic problems. They include variability in quality, weak continuity between pre-university and master’s programs, insufficient use of digital resources, and a shortage of qualified personnel. The main driving force behind the competitiveness of Russian engineering education is the deep, seamless integration of online modules into the learning process and the recruitment of international students, as well as the development of comprehensive educational programs that serve as a scientific and educational boost. Key development prospects include a transition from universal technical programs to a system of individualised educational pathways that takes into account the specifics of future master’s programs, the introduction of active learning methods, and reliance on pedagogical principles of systematicity, scientific approach, and the connection between theory and practice in the design of the information and educational environment.
